props.text:
Commercial Trucks

Commercial trucks depend on reliable braking performance every mile they travel. Whether you’re hauling freight across Florida or making local deliveries, your air brake system is one of the most important safety components on your truck. When even one part begins to wear out or fail, it can lead to longer stopping distances, unexpected downtime, expensive repairs, and failed inspections. Understanding the most common problems with air brake parts can help you recognize issues early and keep your trucks operating safely.

Air leaks are one of the most common problems affecting air brake systems. Leaks often develop from: Worn air lines
Damaged fittings
Cracked hoses
Faulty valves Even a small leak forces the compressor to work harder and can reduce available braking pressure over time. Signs of an air leak include: Constant compressor cycling
Low air pressure warnings
Audible hissing sounds Longer brake application times Ignoring an air leak can quickly turn a minor repair into a much larger problem.
2. Worn Brake Shoes and Brake Drums

Brake shoes naturally wear down every time the brakes are applied. Over time, worn friction material reduces braking performance and places additional stress on the rest of the braking system. Similarly, brake drums can become: Heat checked
Scored
Out of round
Cracked These conditions reduce stopping performance and increase repair costs if left unaddressed. Routine inspections help identify wear before it creates larger safety concerns.

Brake chambers convert compressed air into mechanical force. When diaphragms wear out or chambers become damaged by corrosion, braking force can decrease significantly. Common symptoms include: Uneven braking
Air leaks around the chamber
Reduced stopping power
Parking brake issues Because brake chambers are critical safety components, replacement should always be performed by experienced technicians.

WSlack adjusters help maintain proper brake adjustment. Although automatic slack adjusters reduce maintenance, they still require regular inspection. When slack adjusters fail, drivers may notice: Excessive pushrod travel
Uneven brake wear
Poor braking response
Out-of-service inspection violations Many brake issues that appear to involve other components actually begin with improper adjustment.

Moisture is one of the biggest enemies of any air brake system. That’s why air dryers play such an important role. When air dryers fail, moisture enters the system and causes: Internal corrosion
Frozen air lines during colder weather
Valve failures
Reduced component life Replacing filters and servicing air dryers on schedule helps protect the entire brake system.

Unlike hydraulic braking systems found on passenger vehicles, commercial trucks rely on compressed air to activate the brakes. Because every component works together, a single worn or damaged part can affect the entire system. The primary parts of an air brake system include: ✓ Air compressor
✓ Air dryer
✓ Air tanks
✓ Brake chambers
✓ Slack adjusters
✓ Brake drums and shoes
✓ Valves
✓ Air lines and hoses Routine inspections and preventive maintenance help ensure these components continue performing as designed.
